title: Dynamic batching: sequence-length bucketing and padding minimization
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Continuous batching currently groups requests primarily by arrival window which leads to significant padding overhead on workloads with mixed sequence lengths. This PR introduces a lightweight, sequence-length based bucketing heuristic and padding-minimization policy to improve token throughput and reduce cost without sacrificing latency SLOs.

What this change does: Adds a sequence-length bucketer inside the dynamic batcher that maintains a small set of active buckets (configurable; default 8) keyed by representative length ranges. Incoming requests are placed into the closest-length bucket; batches are closed when either batch size or latency budget is reached. We also add an adaptive padding policy: when a bucket receives a steady stream of short sequences, we enable tighter padding by using per-batch max length estimates and opportunistic KV cache re-use to avoid wasteful padding across the GPU kernels. The heuristic is kept conservative for high-variance buckets to avoid latency regressions.

Files changed (high level): Updated dynamic_batcher core logic to support length buckets and bucket lifecycle; new heuristics module encapsulating bucket selection and padding policy; KV cache manager tweaks to expose fast-paths for same-bucket reuse; added tests and microbenchmarks; short doc on config knobs.

Compatibility & safety: Default behavior preserves existing batcher config if the new feature flag is off. The new bucketing is behind a runtime-config flag (env + console toggle). We keep fallback to the previous batching path for Dedicated/private deployments until rollout is confirmed.

Testing and results: Unit and integration tests added for bucket placement, batch closure conditions, and KV cache reuse. Perf bench harness runs showed consistent improvements on mixed-length traces: p50/p95 latency unchanged (within noise), p99 latency unchanged for latency-heavy profiles, average padding overhead reduced by ~18-22% across traces, token throughput +7% on mixed-length model workloads, and end-to-end cost per token improvement ~5%. CI includes perf gate (local benchmark) and nightly regression checks.

Rollout plan: Feature flag disabled by default; gradual rollout to 10% of traffic on hosted, then 50% after 48h monitoring. Dedicated customers can enable via console config in the next release. Observability: new per-bucket metrics (bucket_count, avg_padding_tokens, bucket_fill_latency) and alert thresholds added to the Console dashboards.

Related: ENG-3721 (batcher refactor), ENG-3735 (kv-cache fast-path), references to previous PRs that experimented with per-seqlen batching heuristics.

Notes: The heuristic parameters (num_buckets, pad_threshold, max_bucket_wait_ms) are tunable and documented in docs/perf/dynamic-batching.md. This PR focuses on heuristic and correctness; further kernel-level packing optimizations will follow in a follow-up PR.

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Nice clean split between bucketing logic and batcher. Concern: are 8 buckets enough for extreme long-tail workloads? Suggest exposing num_buckets and adding diagnostics.
Asha Patel (author): We keep bucket count tunable; added per-bucket metrics and doc about tuning. For long-tail, heuristic falls back to conservative padding and earlier batch closure to protect p99.
Eve Zhang: Please add a safety guard that disables reuse fast-path when model uses mutable KV semantics (SFT-style). Also ensure we don't accidentally reuse KV across model-version rollouts.
Asha Patel: Added explicit model-version check and a runtime guard for mutable KV. Updated tests to cover rollout case.
Darius Kline: Observability looks good, suggest one more perf run on a 2kQPS mixed-length trace before merge.
Asha Patel: Added additional perf runs to CI perf-gate and included aggregated numbers in PR description.
Miguel Santos: Approved after changes. Eve Zhang: Approved. Darius Kline: Approved.
summary_perf: Mixed-length benchmark: avg padding tokens reduced 18-22%; token throughput +7%; p99 latency unchanged for latency-sensitive profiles; cost per token reduced ~5%.
release_notes: Improved dynamic batching: sequence-length bucketing and padding minimization to reduce padding waste and improve throughput on mixed-length workloads. Feature behind runtime flag. Adds per-bucket metrics for observability.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated by runtime flag; monitor new metrics: bucket_count, avg_padding_tokens, bucket_fill_latency. Rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 48h observation windows. If p99 regresses, disable feature flag and investigate bucket distribution.
